newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta PM says committed to neutrality.
newsitem.headline: Malta PM says committed to neutrality.

text.p: Malta's new prime minister Alfred Sant said on Friday he was committed to a policy of neutrality that would not antagonise Western Europe or North Africa.

Sant, heading Malta's first Labour government since 1987, told Reuters:"We don't want to get too close to Western Europe and be perceived as a threat by North Africa, and we don't want to get too close to North Africa and be perceived as a threat by Western Europe.
"We want to have good relations with our neighbours to the north and the south. That way we can contribute to the stability of the central Mediterranean.

Sant had already declared on his election in late October that his government would not proceed with Malta's application to join the European Union and would pull out of the NATO Partnership for Peace programme.
Sant said in an interview it did not make sense for Malta to join the EU in the forseeable future but added -- "of course you never say never."
He said Malta would follow EU regulations at its own pace and was already having informal discussions with Brussels.

He said his island state off the coast of North Africa wanted to have an industrial free trade zone with the EU. Sant said his new government was working on a two-year plan to stabilise Malta's finances.
It wanted to rein-in government spending and push for growth in the private sector, particularly the tourism industry which would be helped by Labour's plan to drop 15 per cent value added tax.
He said his Labour government aimed to promote sustainable economic growth so Malta would not be susceptible to a boom-bust cycle.
